previous_assumption: Assumed restricting the new RequirementService.updateRequirement to status === 'open' was sufficient protection, mirroring how other term-changing actions in this codebase are gated by lifecycle status alone.
correction: 'open' doesn't distinguish "nobody has acted on this yet" from "the market has already responded" — a Renter can currently edit a Requirement's commercial terms (capacity, dates, quantity, etc.) after one or more Rental Companies have already submitted a QuotationResponse against the original terms, or after an Auction has already been created against it, with no notification to the existing responder/participant that terms changed underneath them. This is the same class of gap CommercialQuotation.updateTerms and Rental.updateRentalTerms already close (both clear/restrict on a later-stage action) but RequirementService.updateRequirement does not. Documented in docs/backend-hardening-report.md rather than fixed — a product decision is needed on whether to block the edit once responded-to, or notify existing responders instead.

previous_assumption: createRequirement passed the caller-supplied projectName/projectLocation text straight into the requirement row, asking the Renter to type the same name and location the Project entity (selected via the now-required projectId) already carries.
correction: Client-reported UX bug, root-caused via the codebase's own comment in project contract file stating Project replaces these free-text strings on Requirement/Rental -- an unfinished migration, not a design choice. Removed the two inputs from Post/Edit Requirement dialogs and from createRequirementRequestSchema entirely (projectId is now the only way to say which project). createRequirement already resolved the real Project record to validate projectId -- changed it to snapshot project.project_name/project.site_location onto the requirement automatically instead of trusting removed caller input. The requirement's own project_name/project_location columns still matter and were kept: they are how a Rental Company sees project context in the cross-tenant Open Market view, which has no access to a Renter's own Project records. Scoped deliberately to Requirement only -- Rental has the identical leftover fields but no projectId at all, a separate bigger job.
